claims.explanation: GW-583340 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 kinase inhibitor, so selective killing is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling rather than by a single mutation class. The most sensitive lines include EGFR-mutant or ERBB2/ERBB3-altered tumors and several squamous/adenocarcinoma lines with RTK/PI3K pathway activation, while resistant lines are enriched for RAS/BRAF-driven melanoma, glioma, and KRAS-mutant lung/pancreatic models that bypass EGFR/ERBB2 blockade. Thus high EGFR/ERBB2 pathway activity, especially with EGFR mutation/amplification or ERBB2/ERBB3 alterations, predicts sensitivity, whereas downstream MAPK activation via BRAF/KRAS/NF1 confers protection.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC line HCC4006 is selectively killed; EGFR is the primary drug target
ERBB2 is a direct target and ERBB2-dependent breast/gastric lines are among sensitive
ERBB3 alterations can drive ERBB2/ERBB3-dependent PI3K signaling in sensitive endometrial/breast lines
KRAS-mutant lung, pancreatic, and colorectal lines are enriched among least affected
BRAF-mutant melanoma, glioma, and thyroid lines are predominantly resistant
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in several resistant lines
PTEN loss with downstream PI3K activation is common in resistant melanoma/glioma lines
PIK3CA-mutant bladder, breast, and endometrial lines are among sensitive, suggesting PI3K dependence
TP53 mutation is widespread and not selective, but many resistant lines carry TP53 alterations
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lung, pancreatic, and thyroid lines
STK11-mutant lung and other lines are enriched among least affected
MET alteration may provide bypass RTK signaling in resistant lines
